standfirst: HIV-1 is by far the largest module in this project: 30,530 whole genomes, against 1,324 for every other lentivirus combined. It is separated from HIV-2 and the simian immunodeficiency viruses on layout rather than distance — the two differ by one accessory gene, vpu here against vpx there — which is this project's partitioning rule.

modules.HIV1: tat and rev are not profiled. Both are assembled from two exons far apart on the genome, so neither is collinear with any genomic ORF and a profile built from the deposited protein would be trained to find something the genome does not contain. They are called instead by get_splice_variant_features.pl from reference sets built at an 85% identity gate: at the 95% gate first tried, the references admitted only 41.8% of genomes, and TAT and REV were being dropped for lack of a reference rather than for lack of a gene.

gaps: POL carries no copy_num while the other seven profiled features do. The remaining misses are concentrated in genomes that are incomplete at one end rather than in any one clade. Rates here are per exemplar, not per deposit, which matters more for this module than for any other in the project: 30,530 genomes reduce to 12,985 distinct sequences, so an unweighted rate over raw holdings would largely report how often a sequence was submitted.
